note: Hand-written by WS-K. Openings/CTAs/drafts are fresh text; every item is copy-guarded and fact-guarded by bin/intel/caption_style.py analyse. model_knowledge bullets are NOT measured.

scores_notes.human: The Burmese block is the most human part of every v1 post: spoken endings with ရှင့်, the diminutive လေး, natural English code-mixing (Page, Messenger, PayPay) and the page's own past-post phrases (colloquial spelling ပီး). Its problems are mechanical rather than "AI": the same footer in every post, the Messenger CTA sentence twice in some pattern posts, and an em dash + Japanese gloss (再入荷待ち) in the sold-out line.

en.name: English
en.source_note: All English human samples are TikTok captions by Nepali-audience sellers in Japan (official oEmbed); no English Facebook/Instagram shop captions collected yet.

register_tone: Small shops on Facebook/Instagram write plain first-person English ("we", "you"), short lines and contractions: it reads like a message, not an ad.
hooks: First line = what it is + why now (code, colour, "back in stock", price), because Facebook folds everything after about three lines behind "See more".
price_cta: Price as a number ("¥1,595"); CTA as one verb + one channel ("Message us to order"). "DM for price" annoys buyers.
delivery_stock: Delivery and stock in plain words: "we ship anywhere in Japan", "back in stock", "only 2 left" (only when true).
emoji_hashtags: 0-3 emoji used as signposts (🌸 👉); Facebook needs few or no hashtags, Instagram/TikTok 3-10.
ai_tells: Readers spot AI by em dashes, "elevate / timeless / stunning / whether you're", three-adjective chains, ✨ on every line, title-case banners and "Looking for...?" openers.

do.text: Put code, colour and price in the first line: it is all people see before "See more".
do.basis: measured (n={n}): product named in the first line + model_knowledge

do.text: Keep it short: one idea per line, 2-5 lines on Facebook, 1-2 on TikTok.
Plain verbs: "message us", "order on Messenger", "we ship anywhere in Japan".
0-2 emoji as signposts (🌸 👉), never one per line.
2-5 hashtags at the end: product word + shop + one Nepali/Burmese keyword.
Only catalog facts: code, colour, "Hosonuno (100% cotton)", ¥1,595.
Sound like a person: "we", "you", one small human aside.

dont.text: No em dashes, no " · " chains, no title-case banners framed by emoji.
dont.basis: measured (n={n}): none in human captions; v1 EN block uses them

dont.text: No praise filler: stunning, timeless, elevate, "perfect for", "rich colours".
No "Looking for...?" openers.
No 🇯🇵/🇬🇧 translated twins of the same sentence.
No fancy Unicode fonts (𝒩𝐸𝒲): search and screen readers cannot read them.
Never width/length, supplier codes or "best quality" claims.
Never reuse a competitor sentence (copy guard enforces it).

ja.name: Japanese
ja.source_note: No Japanese human captions collected yet (0 samples): every point is model knowledge until owner screenshots arrive.

register_tone: Small Japanese shops write です・ます with soft friendly endings (〜です♪ / 〜ました！ / 〜ですね). Stacked keigo (させていただきます ×3) feels stiff; noun-stacks joined by ・ read like a catalog.
hooks: The first line says what the news is (入荷 / 再入荷 / 色違い / price); many shops add a short seasonal remark (朝晩涼しくなってきましたね).
price_cta: Price as 「1,595円（税込）」 (consumer prices must be shown tax-inclusive). CTA like 「ご注文・ご質問はDM／Messengerからお気軽にどうぞ」.
delivery_stock: Short set phrases: 全国発送 / 代金引換OK / 残りわずか / 完売しました / 再入荷のお知らせ / 数量限定.
emoji_hashtags: 1-3 emoji or symbols (✨🌸♪); on Instagram 5-15 Japanese hashtags at the end (#和柄 #生地 #ハンドメイド #綿100).
ai_tells: AI tells: 唯一無二 / 洗練された / 「〜があなたの毎日を彩ります」, dashes (—), translated-English phrasing, an emoji at the start of every line.

do.text: です・ます + one soft ending (♪ / ！ / ね) per post.
Line 1 = the news (入荷 / 再入荷 / 色違い); one idea per line, blank line between blocks.
Price 「1,595円（税込）」; material only 「綿100%」.
Colours in Japanese words: 青磁色×藍鼠 / 黄土色×グレー / 茶×赤 / 黒.
CTA as a friendly invitation: 「Messengerからお気軽にどうぞ」.
Instagram: 5-15 Japanese hashtags at the end; Facebook: 0-3.
Write Japanese as its own post, not a line-by-line translation of the English.

dont.text: No 体言止め chains like 「同じ柄・2色・税込・…」 (catalog/robot voice).
dont.basis: measured contrast: v1 JA block does this in every post

dont.text: No 🇯🇵/🇬🇧 flag-labelled translation lines.
No stacked keigo (させていただきます ×3, 誠に…).
No AI praise: 唯一無二, 洗練された, 上質な, 「毎日を彩ります」.
No dashes (—), no English-style quotes or colons in sentences.
Never 細布, never width/length, never supplier codes.
Never copy another shop's wording (copy guard: 12 Japanese characters).

my.name: Burmese
my.source_note: No competitor Burmese caption could be collected (Facebook scraping is forbidden and no owner screenshots yet); the only measured Burmese is our own page's human phrases (1 seller).

register_tone: Myanmar Facebook sellers write spoken Burmese (…ပါတယ် / …နော် / …မယ်), not literary Burmese (…သည် / ၏ / ၍ / …ပါသည်), which reads like a news report or a machine translation. Women sellers end lines with ရှင့်/ရှင်, men with ခင်ဗျာ/ဗျ.
address: Customers are addressed warmly: Customer လေးတို့, အစ်မတို့, ညီမလေးတို့; the diminutive လေး (အထည်လေး, အရောင်လေး) is everywhere and sounds friendly.
hooks: Typical first lines: New Arrival, Instock ပြန်ရပါပြီ, ရောက်ပါပြီနော်, ဈေးလျှော့; fancy-font headers (𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐀𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐥) are common but invisible to search.
price_cta: Price as "¥1,595" or "1595 ယန်း"; CTA via Inbox / Page Messenger, "Comment မှာ code ရေးပေးပါ", phone/Viber. Hiding the price ("ဈေးနှုန်း inbox") is common but loses buyers.
delivery_stock: Delivery/payment lines: အိမ်ရောက်ငွေချေ (COD), ဂျပန်တစ်နိုင်ငံလုံး ပို့ပေးပါတယ်, ပို့ခ; stock: Stock နည်းနည်းပဲ ကျန်တော့တယ်, ပြတ်သွားပါပြီ, ပြန်ရောက်ပါပြီ.
script: Since Myanmar's 2019 switch most new posts are Unicode, but Zawgyi still appears from older phones/fonts (Facebook converts some on display). Always publish Unicode.
ai_tells: AI tells in Burmese: literary endings (သည်/၏), flawless formal grammar with no particles, word-for-word English idioms, long praise lists, em dashes.

do.text: Spoken endings …ပါတယ် / …ပါမယ် / …နော် with the page voice ရှင့်/ရှင်.
Code + price in the first 2-3 lines (before "See more").
Mix English shop words in Latin letters: New arrival, Instock, Sold out, Order, COD.
Warm address: Customer လေးတို့ / အစ်မတို့; diminutive လေး.
Clear price "¥1,595"; COD + delivery-in-Japan line.
2-5 emoji, hearts are fine (🥰💕✨🌸).
Unicode only (checked by the Zawgyi heuristic before anything is saved).

dont.text: No literary register (သည် / ၏ / ၍ / မည် / ပါသည်).
No em dashes or Japanese glosses (再入荷待ち) inside Burmese lines.
dont.basis: measured contrast with v1 sold-out line

dont.text: Don't repeat the same CTA sentence twice in one post.
Don't hide the price behind "inbox".
No Zawgyi, no mixed encodings.
Never length/width (မီတာ) or supplier codes.
Never copy another seller's sentences (copy guard: 20 Burmese characters).

ne.name: Nepali
ne.source_note: Nepali-language samples are romanized-Nepali TikTok captions; script-choice metrics use every caption from Nepali-audience accounts (any body language).

register_tone: Nepali sellers in Japan write like chat: English product words + romanized Nepali glue (ko lagi, cha/xa, garnus, hola) with loose spelling. Devanagari is used more by sellers in Nepal and for keywords.
address: Polite but friendly: dai / didi / sathi haru, hajur in replies; polite imperatives -nus / -nu hola (order garnus, msg garnu hola).
hooks: Openers: "Naya stock aayo", "Japanese lungi available", price first ("¥1,600 matra"), and festival hooks before Dashain/Tihar (koseli = a gift to take home).
price_cta: Price plainly with "matra" (only) or "fixed price"; CTA: inbox / msg garnus, comment, call/Viber; Japanese politeness in romaji (onegaishimasu) also appears.
delivery_stock: "Japan bhari delivery", "COD (daibiki) milcha", "stock limited cha", "sold out bhayo", "feri aayo".
ai_tells: AI tells: Sanskritized formal Devanagari (प्रियजन, उत्तम, उपलब्ध छ), em dashes, perfectly parallel sentences, rhetorical "खोज्दै हुनुहुन्छ?" openers.

do.text: Write mostly English + romanized Nepali; Devanagari for 1-2 keywords or hashtags (#कोसेली).
do.basis: measured (Nepali-audience n={n_aud}): body English or romanized, Devanagari only in hashtags

do.text: Name the product the way buyers search: "Japanese lungi".
Price plainly: "¥1,595 matra".
One-line CTA: "Messenger ma msg garnus".
Dashain/Tihar koseli hooks in season (Oct-Nov).
1-3 emoji (🙏🎁), short lines.
Warmth via dai / didi / sathi haru, hajur.

dont.text: No formal Sanskritized Devanagari sentences (प्रियजन, उत्तम, उपलब्ध छ).
dont.basis: measured (n={n_aud}): 0 Devanagari body text; v1 NE line is formal

dont.text: No em dashes, no flag-labelled translation lines.
Don't claim "original/guaranteed": state facts (100% cotton, price).
No long paragraphs: competitors use 1 line.
Never promise delivery to Nepal or prices in रु: not stated anywhere in our data.
Never width/length or supplier codes.
Never reuse competitor wording or their shop hashtags.
